claim: HSV-2 is shed episodically in the genital tract, leading to occasional genital ulcers and efficient transmission.
source_text: Herpes simplex virus-2 (HSV-2) is shed episodically, leading to occasional genital ulcers and efficient transmission.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about HSV-2 infection patterns.

claim: The biology explaining highly variable shedding patterns in an infected person over time is poorly understood.
source_text: The biology explaining highly variable shedding patterns, in an infected person over time, is poorly understood.
evidence_reasoning: This represents a gap in scientific understanding acknowledged by the authors.

claim: HSV-2 spread locally within single ulcers to thousands of epithelial cells in less than 12 hours in simulations.
source_text: In simulations, HSV-2 spread locally within single ulcers to thousands of epithelial cells in <12 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the mathematical model simulations based on empirical data fitting.

claim: Host immune responses eliminated infected cells in less than 24 hours in simulations.
source_text: host immune responses eliminated infected cells in <24 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model based on fitting to clinical data.

claim: Secondary ulcers formed following spatial propagation of cell-free HSV-2, allowing for episode prolongation.
source_text: secondary ulcers formed following spatial propagation of cell-free HSV-2, allowing for episode prolongation
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by model simulations that reproduce clinical observations.

claim: HSV-2 infection is characterized by extremely rapid virological growth and containment at multiple contemporaneous sites within genital epithelium.
source_text: We conclude that HSV-2 infection is characterized by extremely rapid virological growth and containment at multiple contemporaneous sites within genital epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main conclusion drawn from both empirical data and mathematical modeling.

claim: For disseminated infections, sampling from blood may reflect true host-pathogen dynamics due to homogeneous mixing of viruses and PBMCs.
source_text: For disseminated infections, sampling from blood may reflect true host–pathogen dynamics due to homogeneous mixing of viruses and PBMCs, which originate from thousands of infectious foci.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established understanding of systemic viral infection dynamics.

claim: Many infections are confined to small anatomic regions where localized host-pathogen interactions constitute the predominant site of pathogenesis.
source_text: However, many infections are confined to small anatomic regions; localized host–pathogen interactions within specific organ tissue constitutes the predominant site of pathogenesis
evidence_reasoning: This is general knowledge about localized infections contrasted with disseminated infections.

claim: HSV-2 replicates in highly accessible genital keratinocytes.
source_text: HSV-2 replicates in highly accessible genital keratinocytes.
evidence_reasoning: This is established biological knowledge about HSV-2 tropism.

claim: Serial genital swabbing reveals frequent, highly variable shedding episodes in most infected persons.
source_text: Serial genital swabbing reveals frequent, highly variable shedding episodes in most infected persons
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple cited studies (Wald et al., 1995, 1997, 2000; Crespi et al., 2007; Mark et al., 2008).

claim: Biopsies show dense clusters of CD4+ and CD8+ lymphocytes in focal areas of viral replication.
source_text: biopsies show dense clusters of CD4+ and CD8+ lymphocytes in focal areas of viral replication
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies (Zhu et al., 2007).

claim: Some HSV-2 episodes are associated with lesions and prolonged viral production, while others are asymptomatic and brief.
source_text: Some episodes are associated with lesions, and prolonged viral production, while others are asymptomatic and brief
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited study (Mark et al., 2008).

claim: Markedly different episodes occur within 5-10 days of each other in HSV-2 infected individuals.
source_text: Markedly different episodes occur within 5–10 days of each other
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited study (Mark et al., 2008).

claim: Viral levels fluctuate dramatically even within a single HSV-2 episode.
source_text: viral levels fluctuate dramatically even within a single episode
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies (Mark et al., 2008; Schiffer et al., 2011).

claim: At least 20% of HSV-2 episodes are notable for complex erratic viral trajectories, including re-expansion phases.
source_text: At least 20% of episodes are notable for complex erratic viral trajectories, including re-expansion phases that represent failure of the immune system to contain replication
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited study (Schiffer et al., 2011).

claim: Past modeling suggests that nearly constant reactivation of HSV in a small percentage of infected ganglionic neurons might account for high frequency of shedding episodes.
source_text: Past modeling suggests that nearly constant reactivation of HSV in a small percentage of infected ganglionic neurons might account for high frequency of shedding episodes
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis from previous modeling work (Schiffer et al., 2009).

claim: Animal and mathematical models predict that varying T-cell responses account for episode heterogeneity.
source_text: Animal and mathematical models predict that varying T-cell responses account for episode heterogeneity
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies (Gebhardt et al., 2009; Schiffer et al., 2010).

claim: Absolute mean difference in HSV DNA copies between swabs is a function of time between swabs (R² = 0.99).
source_text: Using data from panel (A and B), absolute mean difference (R2 = 0.99), and (C) mean difference (R2 = 0.87), in HSV DNA copies between swabs, are a function of time between swabs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from the 5-minute sampling data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Mean difference in HSV DNA copies between swabs is a function of time between swabs (R² = 0.87).
source_text: mean difference (R2 = 0.87), in HSV DNA copies between swabs, are a function of time between swabs
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from the 5-minute sampling data.

claim: HSV-2 reactivation occurs simultaneously in multiple regions across the genital tract.
source_text: Based on the observation that HSV-2 reactivation occurs simultaneously in multiple regions across the genital tract
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the spatial sampling data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Probability of episode re-expansion increases as a function of peak episode copy number among 1020 episodes from 531 study subjects.
source_text: Increasing probability of episode re-expansion (nonmonotonic episodes) as a function of peak episode copy number among 1020 episodes from 531 study subjects
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from the large cohort study presented in Figure 2B.

claim: A genital lesion consists of numerous round ulcers clustered in space.
source_text: A genital lesion consists of numerous round ulcers (black dotted circle) clustered in space
evidence_reasoning: This is a clinical observation documented in Figure 2C.

claim: CD8+ T cells at the dermal-epidermal junction are highly localized to ulcer edge (287/mm²) and are fourfold less dense 1 cm away (72/mm²).
source_text: CD8+ T cells (green) at the dermal–epidermal junction (arrow) are highly localized to ulcer edge (287/mm2) and are fourfold less dense 1 cm away (72/mm2)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from immunofluorescent staining of biopsies.

claim: CD8+ T cells form cluster-like aggregates even within a 1-mm biopsy.
source_text: Even within a 1-mm biopsy, CD8+ T cells formed cluster-like aggregates
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from immunofluorescent staining analysis.

claim: Dynamical interactions between acquired immune cells and infected cells occur within tightly spaced microenvironments on a micrometer scale.
source_text: suggesting that dynamical interactions between acquired immune cells and infected cells occur within tightly spaced microenvironments on a micrometer scale
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the spatial distribution patterns of CD8+ T cells observed in biopsies.

claim: Individual ulcers may occur across a wide region of the genital tract during large outbreaks.
source_text: We infer that individual ulcers, both microscopic and visible to the naked eye, may occur across a wide region of the genital tract during large outbreaks.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the spatial distribution of viral shedding and immune responses.

claim: Genital skin and mucosa between ulcers may be relatively quiescent during HSV-2 episodes.
source_text: While each ulcer and microulcer represent a site of intense interface between the virus and T cells, genital skin and mucosa between ulcers may be relatively quiescent.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the localized nature of immune responses observed in biopsies.

claim: The spatial model included 300 regions of 6.5 mm diameter linked in a spatial arrangement of adjacent hexagons.
source_text: Our spatial model included 300 regions of 6.5 mm diameter linked in a spatial arrangement of adjacent hexagons
evidence_reasoning: This describes the structure of the mathematical model developed by the authors.

claim: Cell-associated HSV contributed to ulcer expansion within a region.
source_text: Cell-associated HSV particles contribute to ulcer expansion (white circle) within a region.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis incorporated into the mathematical model.

claim: Cell-free particles initiate secondary ulcers in adjacent regions leading to concurrent ulcers where HSV production occurs.
source_text: Cell-free particles initiate secondary ulcers in adjacent regions (upper right) leading to concurrent ulcers where HSV production occurs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis incorporated into the mathematical model to explain prolonged episodes.

claim: Model output closely reproduced quantitative shedding frequency from empirical data.
source_text: model output closely reproduced the data within Cohort E, including quantitative shedding frequency
evidence_reasoning: This is a validation result showing the model fits the clinical data.

claim: Median initiation to peak expansion rate was 25.5 log10 HSV DNA copies per day in simulated episodes with continuous sampling.
source_text: Among 842 simulated episodes with sampling every 0.001 days, median initiation to peak expansion rate was 25.5 log10 HSV DNA copies per day
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations with high-frequency sampling.

claim: During the early expansion phase, HSV DNA levels increased 10-fold every 57 minutes and doubled every 17 minutes.
source_text: implying that during the early expansion phase, HSV DNA levels increased 10-fold every 57 min and doubled every 17 min
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model's predicted expansion rate.

claim: Number of infected cells and viral load peaked at a median of 13.5 hours in simulated episodes.
source_text: Number of infected cells and viral load peaked at a median of 13.5 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations.

claim: Daily sampling accurately measured quantitative shedding frequency compared to continuous sampling.
source_text: While daily sampling accurately measured quantitative shedding frequency with continuous sampling
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from comparing different sampling frequencies in the model.

claim: More frequent sampling increased episode detection by approximately 50%.
source_text: the model predicted that more frequent sampling increased episode detection by ∼50%
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative prediction from model simulations comparing sampling frequencies.

claim: Approximately 75% of HSV-2 episodes are asymptomatic, brief (<48 hr), and associated with a low peak copy number.
source_text: The model also predicted the finding from Cohort C that ∼75% of HSV-2 episodes are asymptomatic, brief (<48 hr), and associated with a low peak copy number
evidence_reasoning: This is a model prediction that matches empirical findings from Cohort C (Mark et al., 2008).

claim: Epidermal cells produced 72,000-170,000 HSV DNA copies per day according to parameter estimates.
source_text: Epidermal cells produced 72,000–170,000 HSV DNA copies per day
evidence_reasoning: This is a parameter estimate derived from model fitting to empirical data.

claim: One of 76-123 cell-associated DNA particles infected a neighboring cell per day at ulcer onset.
source_text: one of 76–123 cell-associated DNA particles infected a neighboring cell per day at ulcer onset
evidence_reasoning: This is a parameter estimate derived from model fitting.

claim: Median times to 100, 1000, and 10,000 total infected cells were 5.6, 8.7, and 12.9 hours, respectively.
source_text: median times to 100, 1000, and 10,000 total infected cells were 5.6, 8.7, and 12.9 hr, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations of severe episodes.

claim: Median time interval from becoming infected to infecting a new cell during the expansion phase was 6.8 hours.
source_text: Median time interval from becoming infected to infecting a new cell during the expansion phase of the 100 simulated episodes was 6.8 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations.

claim: Median time from becoming infected to infecting a first surrounding cell was 59 minutes.
source_text: median time from becoming infected to infecting a first surrounding cell was 59 min
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations.

claim: In vivo, an HSV-infected keratinocyte might become locally infectious by spreading the virus even before replication initiates within this cell.
source_text: Our data suggest that in vivo an HSV-infected keratinocyte might become locally infectious by spreading the virus even before replication initiates within this cell
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis inferred from the rapid cell-to-cell spread rates predicted by the model.

claim: Episode duration was a function of total ulcers in 500 simulated episodes.
source_text: In 500 simulated episodes, duration was a function of total ulcers
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from model simulations showing the relationship between ulcer number and episode duration.

claim: Cell-free HSV was approximately 2000-fold less infectious than cell-associated HSV according to parameter estimates.
source_text: Parameter estimates suggest that cell-free HSV was ∼2000-fold less infectious than cell-associated HSV
evidence_reasoning: This is a parameter estimate derived from model fitting to empirical data.

claim: Median time to death of 10,000, 1000, or 100 infected cells was 13.7, 9.7, or 6.9 hours, respectively.
source_text: the median time to death of 10,000, 1000, or 100 infected cells was 13.7, 9.7, or 6.9 hr, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations showing rapid immune clearance.

claim: CD8+ T-cell density within the initially infected region was the most predictive parameter of episode peak viral load and duration.
source_text: CD8+ T-cell density within the initially infected region was the most predictive parameter of episode peak viral load and duration.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from global sensitivity analysis of the model.

claim: Increased viral replication rate in epidermal cells and decreased CD8+ T-cell expansion rate correlated with higher peak viral production.
source_text: Increased viral replication rate in epidermal cells and decreased CD8+ T-cell expansion rate also correlated with higher peak viral production
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from sensitivity analysis of model parameters.

claim: Increased viral infectivity and replication rate correlated with longer episode duration.
source_text: while increased viral infectivity and replication rate correlated with longer episode duration
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from sensitivity analysis of model parameters.

claim: Local T-cell density at the site of neuronal HSV-2 release into genital skin determines short-term viral trajectories.
source_text: These findings suggest that local T-cell density at the site of neuronal HSV-2 release into genital skin determines short-term viral trajectories.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from sensitivity analysis and model simulations.

claim: Episodes of greater than 10 days occurred when large genital tract areas were at low CD8+ T-cell density (R > 1).
source_text: Episodes of >10 days occurred when large genital tract areas were at low CD8+ T-cell density (R > 1)
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from model simulations examining prolonged episodes.

claim: CD8+ T-cell and reproductive number spatial patterns cycle intermittently over years.
source_text: Over years, CD8+ T-cell and reproductive number spatial patterns cycled intermittently
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from long-term model simulations.

claim: HSV causes a chronic dynamic inflammatory state in the genital tract.
source_text: suggesting that HSV causes a chronic dynamic inflammatory state in the genital tract
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the cycling patterns of immune responses observed in long-term simulations.

claim: Genital shedding trends were unchanged if HSV was released continuously or in daily, every 3-day, or weekly pulses, provided that the average HSV DNA release rate remained approximately 82/day.
source_text: genital shedding trends were unchanged if HSV was released continuously or in daily, every 3-day, or weekly pulses, provided that the average HSV DNA release rate remained ∼82/day
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from model simulations testing different neuronal release patterns.

claim: HSV release must occur randomly throughout the genital tract to reproduce observed shedding patterns.
source_text: and that release occurred randomly throughout the genital tract
evidence_reasoning: This is a requirement identified through model fitting to reproduce empirical data.

claim: Predictors of elevated shedding rate included high neuronal release rate of HSV-2 DNA, high CD8+ T-cell replication rate, high regional co-dependence of CD8+ T-cell density, low HSV-2 DNA replication rate in skin cells, and low free-viral decay rate.
source_text: Predictors of elevated shedding rate included high neuronal release rate of HSV-2 DNA, high CD8+ T-cell replication rate, high regional co-dependence of CD8+ T-cell density, low HSV-2 DNA replication rate in skin cells, and low free-viral decay rate
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from global sensitivity analysis of 10-year simulations.

claim: Parameter levels that favor immune control in the mucosa correlate with higher long-term shedding rates due to complex nonlinear dynamics.
source_text: The finding that parameter levels which would appear to favor immune control in the mucosa, in fact correlate with higher long-term shedding rates, highlight the complex nonlinear dynamics of the spatial model
evidence_reasoning: This is a counterintuitive finding from sensitivity analysis that reveals model complexity.

claim: Conditions of high CD8+ T-cell replication rate and low HSV-2 DNA replication rate in keratinocytes favor both a higher proportion of very brief episodes (<1 day) and more severe episodes that spread to multiple regions.
source_text: Therefore, conditions of high CD8+ T-cell replication rate and low HSV-2 DNA replication rate in keratinocytes tend to favor both a higher proportion of very brief episodes (<1 day) and more severe episodes that spread to multiple regions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic explanation derived from sensitivity analysis results.

claim: HSV-2 expansion and decay phases in mucosa are considerably more rapid and complex than those of HIV and hepatitis B.
source_text: Viral loads are stable over periods of minutes but can change dramatically over hours. HSV-2 expansion and decay phases in mucosa are considerably more rapid and complex than those of HIV and hepatitis B, which have been characterized by sampling plasma
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative statement based on the current study's findings and cited literature on HIV and hepatitis B dynamics.

claim: HSV replication within epithelial cells and spread by cell-to-cell transfer occur extremely rapidly and efficiently.
source_text: HSV replication within epithelial cells, and spread by cell-to-cell transfer, seem to occur extremely rapidly and efficiently.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the rapid kinetics observed in model simulations.

claim: The immune response becomes dominant only approximately 13.5 hours after HSV-2 detection.
source_text: The model predicts that >108 viral DNA genomes can be produced in one ulcer, even though the immune response becomes dominant only ∼13.5 hr after HSV-2 detection.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations.

claim: Routes of spread between tightly packed epithelial cells might include transit through tight cellular junctions, distant propulsion when cells violently lyse, and homogenous mixing with susceptible cells as a result of high viral titers packed inside herpetic vesicles.
source_text: Routes of spread between tightly packed epithelial cells might include transit through tight cellular junctions (Collins and Johnson, 2003; Farnsworth and Johnson, 2006), distant propulsion when cells violently lyse, and homogenous mixing with susceptible cells as a result of high viral titers packed inside herpetic vesicles
evidence_reasoning: This proposes multiple mechanisms based on cited literature and biological reasoning.

claim: The model is in agreement with mouse studies showing that tissue-resident CD8+ T-cell density at the site of viral challenge dictates lesion severity.
source_text: The model is in agreement with mouse studies, which show that tissue-resident CD8+ T-cell density at the site of viral challenge dictates lesion severity
evidence_reasoning: This compares model predictions with cited animal studies (Gebhardt et al., 2009; Shin and Iwasaki, 2012).

claim: Local CD8+ T-cell count supersedes all other parameters of viral replication and immunologic response in determining the extent of shedding during an episode.
source_text: and further suggests that local CD8+ T-cell count supersedes all other parameters of viral replication and immunologic response in determining the extent of shedding during an episode
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from sensitivity analysis showing CD8+ T-cell density as the dominant parameter.

claim: Most shedding episodes are contained within hours, when less than 10 cells are infected.
source_text: Most shedding episodes are contained within hours, when <10 cells are infected
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by model predictions and cited previous work (Schiffer et al., 2009).

claim: Even if thousands of epithelial cells get infected in an ulcer, these cells appear to be eliminated in less than 24 hours.
source_text: Yet, even if thousands of epithelial cells get infected in an ulcer, these cells appear to be eliminated in <24 hr.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from model simulations of severe episodes.

claim: Cell-free viruses seed adjacent regions where T-cell density may be lower, leading to the formation of secondary foci of viral replication.
source_text: Our model suggests that cell-free virus plays an important role in episode prolongation: cell-free viruses seed adjacent regions where T-cell density may be lower, leading to the formation of secondary foci of viral replication
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by model simulations.

claim: The spatial dynamic between virus and host defines episode morphology and explains variability in shedding severity in an individual over periods of hours to weeks.
source_text: Thus, the spatial dynamic between virus and host defines episode morphology, and explains variability in shedding severity in an individual over periods of hours to weeks.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the spatial model's ability to reproduce observed variability.

claim: Antiviral therapies which only impact intracellular replication do not eliminate prolonged episodes.
source_text: These results suggest that studies of neutralizing and antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity responses in localized mucosal areas are needed, and may explain why antiviral therapies which only impact intracellular replication and do not eliminate prolonged episodes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis about therapeutic implications based on the model's predictions about cell-free virus spread.

claim: A heterogeneous spatial array of immune cell densities at episode onset may determine the complex trajectory of a shedding episode.
source_text: A heterogeneous spatial array of immune cell densities at episode onset may determine the complex trajectory of a shedding episode
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic explanation inferred from model behavior.

claim: When the model was simulated over 30-day intervals, there was heterogeneity in the shedding rate based solely on randomness of episode initiation and high variability of episode duration.
source_text: When we simulated the model over 30-day intervals typically used in our clinical studies, there was heterogeneity in the shedding rate based solely on randomness of episode initiation and high variability of episode duration.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from model simulations examining short-term variability.

claim: Enhanced immune function in the form of lower viral replication rate or viral infectivity has the short-term effect of limiting episode duration.
source_text: Surprisingly, while enhanced immune function in the form of lower viral replication rate or viral infectivity has the predictable short-term effect of limiting episode duration
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from sensitivity analysis of model parameters.

claim: Sustained higher T-cell CD8+ replication rate and lower viral replication rate might counterintuitively increase long-term shedding rates.
source_text: the model suggests that sustained higher T-cell CD8+ replication rate and lower viral replication rate might counterintuitively increase long-term shedding rates
evidence_reasoning: This is a counterintuitive finding from long-term sensitivity analysis.

claim: For the model to precisely recapitulate episode rate, it is necessary to assume a nearly constant slow drip of HSV-2 from neurons.
source_text: For the model to precisely recapitulate episode rate, it is necessary to assume a nearly constant slow drip of HSV-2 from neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is a requirement identified through model fitting and cited previous work (Schiffer et al., 2009).

claim: There is diffuse dispersal of virus from neurons into genital epithelia, rather than focal reactivations only within certain microregions.
source_text: The stochastic model and spatial shedding data both suggest that there is diffuse dispersal of virus from neurons into genital epithelia, rather than focal reactivations only within certain microregions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from both model requirements and spatial shedding observations.

claim: The vast majority of HSV within ganglia is maintained in a low copy number latent state, while a minority reactivates on a frequent basis.
source_text: Rather, we favor the idea that the vast majority of HSV within ganglia is maintained in a low copy number latent state (Wang et al., 2005; Verjans et al., 2007), while a minority reactivates albeit on a frequent basis.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis based on cited literature and model requirements.

claim: Most HSV-2 transmissions occur when an infected person is asymptomatic.
source_text: Most transmissions occur when an infected person is asymptomatic
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies (Mertz et al., 1985, 1998).

claim: Secondary seeding starts to predictably occur in modeled episodes when viral loads in a single ulcer exceed 10^6 HSV DNA copies.
source_text: Secondary seeding starts to predictably occur in modeled episodes when viral loads in a single ulcer exceed 106 HSV DNA copies.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations.

claim: At viral loads of 10^6 HSV DNA copies, there are roughly 1000 dead cells, which is not enough for a microulcer to become visible to the naked eye.
source_text: At this viral load, there are roughly 1000 dead cells, which is not enough for a microulcer to become visible to the naked eye.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model's relationship between viral load and cell death.

claim: HSV-2 can efficiently seed new regions across the genital tract leading to prolonged high copy number episodes even when shedding is not associated with lesions.
source_text: Therefore, HSV-2 can efficiently seed new regions across the genital tract leading to prolonged high copy number episodes even when shedding is not associated with lesions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion about asymptomatic transmission drawn from model predictions.

claim: The model underestimates immunologic complexity by assuming CD8+ T-cell response is a surrogate of the entire immune response.
source_text: Hence, one limitation is that the model underestimates immunologic complexity. CD8+ T-cell response is assumed to be a surrogate of the entire immune response.
evidence_reasoning: This is an acknowledged limitation of the model stated by the authors.

claim: Other key cellular subsets such as CD4+ lymphocytes, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells are not included in the model.
source_text: Other key cellular subsets such as CD4+ lymphocytes, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells are not included.
evidence_reasoning: This is an acknowledged limitation of the model.

claim: Lack of inclusion of innate immunity is a shortcoming as interferon type 1 is present early during lesions and contributes to episode containment.
source_text: Lack of inclusion of innate immunity is another shortcoming as interferon type 1 is present early during lesions (Spruance et al., 1982), and contributes to episode containment.
evidence_reasoning: This is an acknowledged limitation with reference to cited literature.

claim: Chronic HSV-2 infection leads to a dynamic and spatially heterogeneous state of immune readiness.
source_text: Our model generates the hypothesis that chronic HSV-2 infection leads to a dynamic and spatially heterogeneous state of immune readiness.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis generated from long-term model simulations.

claim: If swabs only remove a fixed proportion of free-viral DNA, then the study may be underestimating the genital tract viral load.
source_text: If swabs only remove a fixed proportion of free-viral DNA, then it is possible that we are underestimating the genital tract viral load.
evidence_reasoning: This is a potential limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: By rapidly spreading between epidermal cells, HSV-2 ensures high viral production within a single ulcer, despite an intense local immune response.
source_text: Our model raises the possibility that by rapidly spreading between epidermal cells, HSV-2 ensures high viral production within a single ulcer, despite an intense local immune response.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis about viral strategy inferred from model behavior.

claim: Cell-free HSV-2 may prolong episodes via spread to contiguous sites where immune cell density is lower.
source_text: Cell-free HSV-2 may prolong episodes via spread to contiguous sites where immune cell density is lower.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by model simulations.

claim: Viral strategies that lead to repeated episodes, rapid episode expansion and frequent re-expansion, allow for high shedding frequency, thereby enhancing transmission and disease manifestations.
source_text: Viral strategies that lead to repeated episodes, rapid episode expansion and frequent re-expansion, allow for high shedding frequency, thereby enhancing transmission and disease manifestations.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion about viral evolutionary strategy inferred from model predictions.

claim: Interventions that target spread of virus between epidermal cells in a single ulcer, and to new regions of the genital tract, will be of value in controlling HSV-2 infection.
source_text: Interventions that target spread of virus between epidermal cells in a single ulcer, and to new regions of the genital tract, will be of value in controlling HSV-2 infection.
evidence_reasoning: This is a therapeutic recommendation based on model insights.

claim: HSV DNA was detected using a quantitative PCR assay expressed as copies per milliliter of medium.
source_text: HSV DNA was detected using a quantitative PCR assay, and was expressed as copies per milliliter of medium.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the measurement method used in the study.

claim: The PCR assay uses type-common primers to the HSV gene encoding glycoprotein B.
source_text: The PCR assay uses type-common primers to the HSV gene encoding glycoprotein B.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the technical details of the PCR assay.

claim: An internal control was included to ensure that HSV-negative swabs were not due to inhibition.
source_text: An internal control was included to ensure that HSV-negative swabs were not due to inhibition.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a quality control measure in the PCR assay.

claim: Cohort E participants swabbed their entire genital tract every 24 hours for a minimum of 30 days.
source_text: Cohort E was used for fitting the model (Schiffer et al., 2011): participants swabbed their entire genital tract every 24 hr whether lesions were present or not for a minimum of 30 days.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the study protocol for the main fitting cohort.

claim: Cohort C participants swabbed every 6 hours, allowing for more precise measures of episode rate, early episode expansion rate, and late episode decay rate.
source_text: Cohort C was similar to Cohort E, except participants swabbed every 6 hr (Mark et al., 2008), allowing for more precise measures of episode rate, early episode expansion rate, and late episode decay rate.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the study protocol and rationale for Cohort C.

claim: At least 10% of CD8+ T cells detected in tissue at the dermal-epidermal junction are HSV-2 specific and this proportion remains constant as CD8+ T-cell levels fluctuate.
source_text: Previous studies indicated that at least 10% of CD8+ T cells detected in tissue at the dermal–epidermal junction are HSV-2 specific and that this proportion remains constant as CD8+ T-cell levels fluctuate
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited previous work (Zhu et al., 2007).

claim: Model 1 failed to create episodes with multiple peaks and failed to produce episodes of greater than 4 days duration.
source_text: Model 1 failed to create episodes with multiple peaks, and failed to produce episodes of >4 days duration (∼33% of clinical episodes)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the limitations of the first model iteration.

claim: In Model 2, cell-associated particles converted to cell-free virus after infected cells ruptured.
source_text: In Model 2, cell-associated particles (Vi) converted to cell-free virus (Ve) after infected cells ruptured.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a feature of the second model iteration.

claim: Model 2 also failed to create episodes with multiple peaks and failed to produce episodes of greater than 4 days duration.
source_text: Model 2 also failed to create episodes with multiple peaks, and failed to produce episodes of >4 days duration
evidence_reasoning: This describes the limitations of the second model iteration.

claim: Model 3 consisted of 300 possible regions of infection, linked by the ability of neurons to randomly release virus into any of the 300 regions.
source_text: Model 3 consisted of 300 possible regions of infection, linked by the ability of neurons to randomly release virus into any of the 300 regions.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the structure of the third model iteration.

claim: Model 3 produced longer episodes in general than Model 2 and successfully created episodes with re-expansion, but episodes were too short in duration to reproduce the frequency histogram for episode duration.
source_text: Model 3 produced longer episodes in general than Model 2, and successfully created episodes with re-expansion. Nevertheless, episodes were too short in duration to reproduce the frequency histogram for episode duration
evidence_reasoning: This describes the performance and limitations of the third model iteration.

claim: Individual cells turn red approximately 12-24 hours after very low multiplicity of infection (MOI = 0.001) of Vero cells.
source_text: Individual cells turn red approximately 12–24 hr after very low multiplicity of infection (MOI = 0.001) of Vero cells
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation from cell culture experiments.

claim: The average surface area of recurrent genital HSV lesions in immunocompetent persons is 60 mm² (range 2-270 mm²).
source_text: We chose this diameter because the average surface area of recurrent genital HSV lesions (which may include many ulcers) in immunocompetent persons is 60 mm2 (range 2–270 mm2)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited study (Corey et al., 1983).

claim: Ulcers are rarely greater than 3 mm in diameter.
source_text: Ulcers are rarely >3 mm in diameter.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as clinical knowledge by the authors.

claim: When fitting with 5 rather than 10 unknown parameters, the sum of squares and AIC scores indicated a very slight decrease in fit to Cohort A data.
source_text: When fitting with 5 rather than 10 unknown parameters, the sum of squares and AIC scores indicated a very slight decrease in fit to Cohort A data
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from comparing different model fitting approaches.

claim: CD8+ T-cell density at episode onset has an important effect on amount of virus produced per episode.
source_text: A feature shared by all models described in this manuscript is sensitivity to CD8+ T-cell density at episode onset, which had an important effect on amount of virus produced per episode
evidence_reasoning: This is a consistent finding across models and cited previous work (Schiffer et al., 2010).

claim: The reproductive number (R) is the average number of cells that an infected cell would infect assuming the presence of CD8+ T cells.
source_text: The reproductive number is the average number of cells that an infected cell would infect assuming the presence of CD8+ T cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of a standard epidemiological parameter adapted to the model.

claim: The loss of 14,400, 57,800, and 130,000 cells at any given point in time will lead to 1-, 2-, and 3-mm-diameter ulcers, respectively.
source_text: Our formula for diameter predicts that the loss of 14,400, 57,800, and 130,000 cells at any given point in time will lead to 1-, 2-, and 3-mm-diameter ulcers, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model's formula relating cell loss to ulcer size.

claim: Noninfectious cell-free HSV, as may occur in the presence of comprehensive neutralizing antibody protection, resulted in a decrease in episode duration and shedding frequency from 18.2% to 10.8%.
source_text: we conducted a 365-day simulation with infectious and noninfectious cell-free HSV DNA (Videos 4 and 5) and found that noninfectious cell-free HSV, as may occur in the presence of comprehensive neutralizing antibody protection, resulted in a decrease in episode duration and shedding frequency from 18.2% to 10.8%.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations testing the role of neutralizing antibodies.

claim: Herpetic lesions rarely form in skin surrounding the genital tract.
source_text: Episodes of >10 days occurred when large genital tract areas were at low CD8+ T-cell density (R > 1) (Video 8). HSV replication sometimes terminated at edge regions, which is biologically realistic because herpetic lesions rarely form in skin surrounding the genital tract.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as clinical knowledge to justify model boundary conditions.

claim: Kissing lesions, in which two ulcers form at the site of skin-to-skin contact, are a well-documented phenomenon.
source_text: 'Kissing lesions', in which two ulcers form at the site of skin-to-skin contact, are a well-documented phenomenon
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established clinical knowledge.

claim: Ulcers do not isolate within genital tract dermatomes as occurs with zoster reactivation.
source_text: On the other hand, ulcers do not isolate within genital tract dermatomes as occurs with zoster reactivation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative clinical observation about HSV-2 vs zoster distribution patterns.

claim: Ulcers tend to be closely arrayed in space rather than widely dispersed across vulnerable regions in the genital tract.
source_text: In addition, ulcers tend to be closely arrayed in space rather than widely dispersed across vulnerable regions in the genital tract.
evidence_reasoning: This is a clinical observation from the spatial sampling studies.

claim: Local seeding from epithelial lesions may be responsible for many secondary ulcers.
source_text: These observations suggest that local seeding from epithelial lesions may be responsible for many secondary ulcers.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the spatial clustering patterns of ulcers.

claim: In HSV replication in cell culture, viral replication does not occur until approximately 12-16 hours after a single cell is infected by a single virus.
source_text: Based on our observation in cell culture that in a single cell infected by a single virus, viral replication does not occur until approximately 12–16 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation from cell culture studies.

claim: In culture, HSV replication occurs within newly infected cells 4-6 hours post-infection.
source_text: This finding was surprising because in culture, HSV replication occurs within newly infected cells 4–6 hr post-infection
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited reference (Roizman, 2007).

claim: CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell densities in the genital skin were maximal at ulcer edge and considerably lower in regions 1 cm away.
source_text: CD8+ and CD4+ T-cell densities in the genital skin were maximal at ulcer edge (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), and considerably lower in regions 1 cm away (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from biopsy analysis.

claim: CD8+ T-cell density at ulcer edge was 132/mm² and CD4+ T-cell density was 447/mm².
source_text: CD8+ T-cells (red) and CD4+ T-cells (green) at the dermal epidermal junction (arrow) are highly localized to ulcer edge (132/mm2 and 447/mm2, respectively)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from immunofluorescent staining.

claim: CD8+ T-cell density 1 cm away from ulcer was 91/mm² and CD4+ T-cell density was 132/mm².
source_text: and are less dense 1 cm away (91/mm2 and 132/mm2, respectively)

claim: Continuous sampling detected 842 episodes (28.1/year) versus 450 episodes (15.0/year) with daily sampling.
source_text: Continuous sampling detected 842 episodes (28.1/year) vs 450 episodes (15.0/year) with daily sampling.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from model simulations comparing sampling frequencies.

claim: The 392 additional episodes detected with continuous sampling were all less than a day in duration and mostly less than 10^4 peak HSV DNA copies.
source_text: The 392 additional episodes were all less than a day in duration and mostly <104 peak HSV DNA copies per milliliter
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding characterizing the additional episodes detected with more frequent sampling.
